items.headline: Nasdaq 100 closes in correction territory, 10.4% below its October 6 record, as chip stocks lead the sell-off
items.why: The drop was concentrated in semiconductors (the Philadelphia chip index fell 3.4% on Nov 2) while most other sectors rose, so the market is repricing whether AI spending will pay off rather than selling everything.

sources.title: The Nasdaq 100 Is Now Officially in a Correction - 24/7 Wall St.

items.headline: Apple beats on revenue ($114.5B, iPhone +17.5%) but guides December-quarter gross margin to 45%-46%, below the 46.3% analysts expected
items.why: Rising memory-chip costs are now squeezing the most profitable hardware maker, a signal that the AI buildout is raising input costs for the whole device industry.

sources.title: Apple earnings beat expectations, but rising chip costs worry investors - Euronews

items.headline: AI heavyweights rebound on Nov 3 while capital rotates toward industrials, healthcare and staples
items.why: A one-day bounce after a correction is not a reversal; the rotation out of heavy AI spenders is the trend to watch if the bounce fails.

sources.title: Nasdaq ends higher as AI heavyweights rebound ahead of midterm results - MarketScreener

items.headline: Binance loses about $6.3 billion in the largest crypto theft on record, roughly four times the previous record
items.why: Around $3 billion was frozen, but the attacker still held coins no issuer can freeze, so a sizeable overhang of potential selling remains.

sources.title: Binance hack: $6.3 billion stolen in largest crypto heist in history - Wealth Professional

items.headline: US spot Bitcoin ETFs post $116 million net outflow on Nov 3, a third straight day of outflows
items.why: Persistent ETF selling removes the main source of marginal institutional demand just as Bitcoin tests its long-term support.

sources.title: Bitcoin spot ETFs see $116M net outflow on Nov 3 - KuCoin News

items.headline: Bitcoin heads into the midterms around $77,000, about 5% above its 200-day average and on pace for a fifth straight weekly loss
items.why: In past midterm years Bitcoin sat well below that average on election day; holding above it is the main evidence this cycle's drawdown is shallower than earlier ones.

sources.title: Bitcoin is breaking a midterm election pattern going back to 2014 - CoinDesk
Live updates: Bitcoin faces fifth weekly loss as midterm uncertainty and Apple warning weigh on markets - CoinDesk

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%-4.00% on a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters wanting a hike; futures price about an 86% chance of a quarter-point hike on December 9
items.why: The next move priced is a rise, not a cut, and the 10-year Treasury yield is back above 5%, which tightens financial conditions for equities and crypto alike.

sources.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady, but December Hike Looms as Treasury Yields Stay Above 5% - Indrastra

items.headline: US job openings jump to 7.52 million in September, well above the 7.15 million expected
items.why: A strong labour market gives the Fed room to hike, raising the stakes for the October jobs report on Nov 6 and CPI on Nov 10.

sources.title: Gold prices struggling as U.S. sees solid rise in job postings - Kitco

items.headline: Iran signals openness to peace talks via Qatar, with separate talks set for Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, while Hormuz shipping stays disrupted
items.why: Roughly a fifth of global oil supply transits the strait, so headlines on these talks are currently driving crude more than inventory data.

sources.title: Brent at $103.60: the peace trade is selling paper, but the physical market just drew 5.3 million barrels - Mitrade

items.headline: Brent settles at $103.60, its lowest close since October 7 and about 8% lower on the week, after hitting $117.64 on October 30
items.why: Oil is trading the diplomacy headlines, but a fifth straight weekly draw in US crude stocks (API data) shows the physical market is still tight.

sources.title: Brent at $103.60: the peace trade is selling paper, but the physical market just drew 5.3 million barrels - Mitrade

items.headline: OPEC+ holds December output targets unchanged for a third straight month; all 21 members meet on November 29 to set 2027 baselines
items.why: The hold had little price impact, so supply policy is not the swing factor until the 2027 baseline decision.

sources.title: Brent Crude $110: Falls 3 Percent After OPEC+ Hold - FinanceFeeds

items.headline: Spot gold trades near $3,938 an ounce, holding support above $3,900 as strong labour data raises Fed-hike odds
items.why: Gold earns no yield, so a hawkish Fed and 5% Treasuries are the main headwind to the metal at present.

sources.title: Gold prices struggling as U.S. sees solid rise in job postings - Kitco

items.headline: Nasdaq 100 closed Nov 2 at 27,989.82, under its 28,102 correction line; the QQQ ETF closed at $681.09, just above its 200-day average of $679.82
items.why: The 200-day average is the line that held on Nov 2; a close below it would show the selling spreading beyond chips.

sources.title: The Nasdaq 100 Is Now Officially in a Correction - 24/7 Wall St.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes Nov 3 at 7,568.92 (+0.36%), ending a three-day losing streak; Nasdaq 100 rebounds to 28,180.26 (+0.68%)
items.why: The Nasdaq 100 is back above its correction line but remains about 10% below its record, so the bounce has not yet repaired the October breakdown.

sources.title: Nasdaq ends higher as AI heavyweights rebound ahead of midterm results - MarketScreener

items.headline: Bitcoin: support $76,400-76,500 (200-day EMA), $75,000-75,600, then $73,200 (200-day SMA); resistance $78,000-78,200, then $79,500; daily RSI near 34
items.why: Price has made lower highs and lower lows since early October, and a weekly close above $83,000 is the level cited as ending that downtrend.

sources.title: Bitcoin Today: Why BTC Slips Toward $76,000 on 3 November - Admirals

items.headline: Brent: support $100, then $97.36 (September neckline); resistance $110, then the $117.64 high
items.why: A break below $97.36 would open the measured downside target near $84.53, close to the roughly $86 no-war reference some models use.

sources.title: Brent at $103.60: the peace trade is selling paper, but the physical market just drew 5.3 million barrels - Mitrade
